CCPWidget + WidgetDescriptor + WidgetRegistry in CCPKit/Widgets. Registry is composed by the app rather than a self-assembling shared instance, so tests stand up fixture registries; re-registering an id replaces it in place so gallery order stays declaration order. WidgetSize is a named enum in CCPKit and the points live in CCPUI. 10 tests.

Status item toggles a borderless non-activating NSPanel at .popUpMenu, canJoinAllSpaces, anchored top-right of visibleFrame (so an auto-hidden menu bar is not a special case). Window and SwiftUI graph built at launch and never torn down. Blur ended up per-card rather than per-panel at the user's direction: the window is transparent and each GlassCard carries its own behind-window NSVisualEffectView, because a panel-wide backdrop reads as a dark container and SwiftUI materials can't blur the desktop. Panel size comes from the hosting view's fittingSize.

CCPUI design system: Space/Radius/Stroke/Layout in Dimensions.swift, a deliberately tiny Palette (semantic aliases over four white/black alphas; everything else is a system colour), GlassCard as the surface and WidgetCard as what a widget writes. A widget is buildable with no spacing, radius or colour literal.

LayoutAutosave: debounced 500ms, the write itself off-main, last layout wins, flushed synchronously when the panel closes or the app quits. Launch no longer writes the layout back at all — with every edit saved, a rewrite nobody asked for is a silent edit of the user's file. Shipped in fb0038c.

Decided: cap, not scroll. Layout.laneCapacity(inWidth:) says how many lanes a display can show; edit mode refuses the drop that would exceed it rather than letting the arrangement grow off-screen. The existing sizeFitting clamp stays as the guardrail for a layout carried over from a wider display. A horizontal scroll was rejected — macOS Control Center never scrolls sideways and the panel is a control surface, not a document. Shipped in fb0038c.
